# Castopod

- Category: open-source host
- Checked: 2026-09-26
- Primary docs: https://docs.castopod.org/

> **Verified 2026-09-26 (P0-03).** This file is the research-pass evidence for one vendor. Pricing, IAB certification and Apple HLS partner cells were rechecked against primary sources; corrections are marked inline. IAB status comes from the [IAB Tech Lab compliance registry](https://iabtechlab.com/compliance-programs/compliant-companies/). Apple's own partner search ([podcastsconnect.apple.com/partner-search](https://podcastsconnect.apple.com/partner-search)) redirects to an Apple ID sign-in, so partner status is attributed to the vendor or trade press, not an Apple list (checked 2026-09-26). The summary and comparison are in [`../vendors.md`](../vendors.md).

## Integration surface

- **API:** REST API, OpenAPI 3.1.0 spec, disabled by default (`restapi.enabled=true` env flag); read endpoints for podcasts/episodes (list/get), write endpoints to add and publish episodes gated by separate Basic Auth (`restapi.basicAuth=true` + credentials). No rate limits documented. [API Overview](https://docs.castopod.org/next/en/api/) (2026-09-26)
- **Webhooks:** None documented.
- **Export formats:** No first-class export feature documented in the public docs. Hands-on (P0-02) confirmed the only path is a raw `mariadb-dump` of the database plus manual copy of the media directory/S3 bucket — not versioned, not GUID-anchored, no CLI export command. [`evaluations/castopod.md`](../castopod.md) W-EXPORT
- **SSO / auth:** No SSO/SAML documented; instance auth is Castopod's own user/role system (Super Admin / Manager / Podcaster) plus per-podcast contributor roles (Admin/Editor/Author/Guest). [Authentication & Authorization](https://docs.castopod.org/main/en/getting-started/auth/) (2026-09-26)
- **Lock-in risks:** (1) No documented bulk/versioned export — getting all data+media out means a raw DB dump plus manual media copy (hands-on confirmed, `evaluations/castopod.md` W-EXPORT). (2) Feed/episode URLs are not stable across slug changes or feed imports — no automatic 301 redirect from old to new paths (hands-on, W-CORR-GUID/W-IMPORT), so moving off Castopod risks breaking existing subscriber URLs. (3) Analytics are proprietary to the instance (self-hosted, IAB v2.0-style but uncertified) with no export API for historical stats beyond manual DB/CSV access. (4) AGPL-3.0: using Castopod unmodified carries no obligation, but modifying and hosting it would require publishing the modified source under AGPL — a real constraint if Relay ever forked it instead of just borrowing ideas (hands-on, `evaluations/castopod.md` AGPL section).

## Narrative (≤150 words)

Castopod's public docs describe a capable single-tenant creator tool: real per-show contributor roles, Podcasting 2.0 namespace coverage (transcript, chapters, person), fediverse-native comments, premium/private feeds, and a disabled-by-default REST API. It has no documented network layer above a single podcast, no approval/review-before-publish gate, no video/HLS support (and is not named in any HLS partner list found), no DAI/programmatic ad tooling, and no first-class data export — only a raw DB dump. Hands-on evaluation (P0-02) sharpens several of these into concrete risks beyond what docs alone show: premium media is effectively public via an unsigned redirect target, download counts are trivially spoofable, slug/import changes break URLs with no redirect, and media replacement isn't versioned. For Relay's needs — multi-show network, editorial approval with an immutable release record, video, human-reviewed transcripts, community, premium feeds, and portable export — Castopod covers community/premium/transcripts at a documentation level but lacks the release-manifest, video, and export primitives Relay requires.

## Research notes

- Docs site has `main` and `next` branches (e.g., `/main/en/` vs `/next/en/api/`); API docs were only found under `/next/en/api/`, suggesting the REST API may be newer/unreleased in the stable branch — flagged, not confirmed either way from docs alone.
- No dedicated Castopod docs page found for dynamic ad insertion/programmatic ads; absence treated as "undocumented," consistent with brief's instruction.
- castopod.com pricing page did not publish per-plan seat/user counts or per-show limits, so the pricing_2_show answer for seats/shows relies on inference from storage/bandwidth tiers only — would need direct vendor confirmation (out of scope per "no contact sales" rule).
- Apple's `podcasters.apple.com/video-apple-podcasts` page does not print an inline partner list (only links to `/partner-search`); partner names were corroborated via third-party reporting (Triton Digital, podnews) rather than a single authoritative Apple list page — labelled third-party accordingly.
- IAB Tech Lab's own compliance/certified-companies listing was not confirmed to be browsable without deeper navigation; relied on Castopod's own blog statement that it is not certified, which is the more authoritative source for a negative claim about Castopod itself.
- v2 plugin architecture (blog posts on the first 12 plugins, plugin repository) was reviewed for the API/extensibility surface but is a pre-release feature per the hands-on evaluation.
